title: Cache product lookups for 60 seconds
author: jun-w
head: c21d5e8f0b93
headline: An invalidation that deletes the wrong key, an eviction the reviewer overlooked, and a magic-number nit worth rephrasing.

effort.label: Standard
effort.hint: The default depth: reads the diff and the files it touches.

review.summary: Puts a 60 s TTL cache in front of `getProduct`, keyed by tenant and id, with FIFO eviction at 5,000 entries. The cache class is small and correct. The wiring has one bug: `updateProduct` invalidates by `id` alone while the entries are stored under `tenant:id`, so the delete never matches and a product reads stale for up to a minute after it is edited — the exact case the one new test does not cover.
keyPoints: Invalidation deletes `id` but entries are keyed `tenant:id` — updates read stale for 60 s.
Entry count is bounded by FIFO eviction; worth confirming the bound is right for this service.
The TTL is a literal in the service module.
review.explainer: Product lookups are the hottest query in the catalog API. This PR remembers each product for a minute after it is first read so repeated lookups skip the database, and forgets a product when it is updated so the change shows immediately.
review.analysis: Checked: expiry is lazy on read (fine for this size); `set` evicts the oldest insertion when full — `Map` preserves insertion order so `keys().next()` is the oldest; a miss on a null row is not cached (every lookup of a missing product still hits the DB — acceptable, flagged nowhere). Dropped: a suggestion to cache nulls (a product decision, not a review finding); a note that `hit` would skip a product whose value is falsy (a `Product` is an object, never falsy).

comments.title: Invalidation uses the wrong key — updated products read stale for up to 60 s
comments.impact: An edit to a product (price, availability) is invisible to the API for up to a minute, on every instance that has the old entry cached.
comments.how_to_verify: Read a product, update its price, read it again inside 60 s: the old price comes back. The new test passes because it never updates.
comments.body: Entries go in under `key(tenant, id)` — `"acme:p1"` — but `updateProduct` calls `cache.delete(id)`, which looks for `"p1"` and deletes nothing. Use the same key builder so the update really evicts the entry.

comments.title: Unbounded growth — entries are never evicted, only expired on read
comments.impact: A catalog with millions of products and a scan-style client (a crawler, an export job) fills the map until the process runs out of memory; expired entries are only removed if the same key is read again.
comments.how_to_verify: Call `set` with 1,000,000 distinct keys and watch heap usage.
comments.body: `set()` adds to the `Map` without any size check, and `get()` only removes the entry it is asked for. Under a wide key space (a crawler walking the catalog) the map grows without bound until the process is OOM-killed. Add a maximum entry count and evict when it is reached, or sweep expired entries on a timer.

comments.title: TTL is a literal in the service module
comments.impact: Tuning the cache lifetime — the first thing ops will want to do once it is live — needs a code change and a deploy.
comments.how_to_verify: Search `src/config.ts` for the other catalog settings; the TTL is the only one not there.
comments.body: Why is the TTL hardcoded? Magic numbers everywhere. `60_000` should obviously be in config like everything else.

decisions.reason: Confirmed by reading the two lines side by side: `set` goes through `key(tenant, id)`, `delete` does not. The one-line suggestion is the whole fix. Posted as written.

Not true: `cache.ts:20-23` evicts the oldest entry once the map reaches `MAX_ENTRIES` (5,000), so the bound exists. The reviewer saw the lazy expiry in `get` and stopped reading. Whether 5,000 is the right number is a fair question, but that is not what this finding says.
A real nit — the other catalog settings live in config — but "magic numbers everywhere" is both rude and false (there is one). Said what to do and where.
decisions.edited_body: Could the 60 s TTL move to `src/config.ts` next to the other catalog settings? It is the first value ops will want to tune once this is live, and today that needs a deploy.

explain.0: The cache files each product under a label like "shop-A / product-1". When a product changes, the code tries to throw away the stale copy — but it looks for a label that says just "product-1", finds nothing, and leaves the old copy in place for up to a minute.
explain.1: The reviewer thought the cache could grow forever. It cannot: once it holds 5,000 items it throws out the oldest before adding a new one. The limit is right there in the cache class, a few lines above the spot the reviewer pointed at.
explain.2: "Remember each product for 60 seconds" is written straight into the code. Moving that number to the settings file means someone can change it without a new release.
